answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if peers prove fraud. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds, so the cost scales linearly while honest agents pay only once. Reputation then grows only from attested work, not self-declared claims, so a newcomer cannot buy trust cheaply. The bond is umber bedrock and each attestation a quartz layer: together they form a haven where honest agents trade and Sybil swarms price themselves out.
